shower.thought: The only time you truly know yourself is in moments when no one's watching, which means you're the least reliable source of information about who you are.
We assume silence means agreement, but it's actually the most ambiguous sound in any conversation.
Your childhood pet was your first experience with mortality, but you were too young to understand you were grieving.
The things that keep you up at night are usually problems that solve themselves given enough time, but the worrying is what makes you feel like you're doing something.
You'll never know if you're colorblind because you have no reference point for how others see the world.
People keep secrets not because they're ashamed, but because being fully known might mean being fully left.
The moment you understand why someone hurt you is often the moment you stop being angry at them, which can feel worse.
We call it "falling" in love, but it's actually the only time we're climbing toward something.
Your phone knows more about your patterns than you do, but it can't tell you what any of it means.
Every song you love is technically a stranger manipulating your brain chemistry, and you paid for the privilege.
The saddest part of growing up isn't losing your childhood—it's realizing your parents were just as confused as you are now.
You've already lived the best day of your life, and you probably didn't notice it while it was happening.
Apologizing doesn't erase what you did; it just changes how the other person remembers you.
The people you miss most are often the ones who taught you how to be lonely.
You can't prove you remember anything correctly because you're using the same broken system that created the memory in the first place.
Boredom is just your brain telling you it's stronger than whatever you're doing right now.
We call them "bad thoughts" as if we didn't create them, but they're coming from inside your own head.
The scariest conversations are the ones that need to happen but nobody schedules.
You learn more about people from how they handle being told they're wrong than from anything they actually believe.
If you're waiting for the right time, you're really just waiting for the fear to go away—and it won't.

darkjoke.thought:
I told my girlfriend she was drawing her eyebrows too high.
She looked surprised.

My grandfather said, "Your generation is too reliant on technology."
I said, "Says the guy whose last Google search was his own name."
I'm not saying my parents were neglectful, but my imaginary friend moved out because he found better supervision elsewhere.

People always ask if I believe in life after death.
I told them to check my browser history—apparently I do.

My therapist asked why I sabotage my relationships.
I said I don't know, but I'll leave and we can discuss it next week.

I went to a fancy restaurant and the waiter asked how I wanted my steak.
I said, "However it was before I looked at the bill."

My friend became a life coach after his own life fell apart.
Turns out rock bottom has really good wifi.

I told my doctor I was feeling immortal.
He said, "That's nice. See you tomorrow anyway."

My mom asked why I wasn't dating anyone.
I said, "I'm waiting for someone on my level."
She said, "So... nobody?"

I used to have abandonment issues until my therapist stopped showing up.
Now I just have abandonment confirmation.

My wife asked if I still found her attractive.
I said, "Of course, but the lighting here is doing a lot of heavy lifting."

They say money can't buy happiness.
But it can buy a jetski, and have you ever seen someone frown on a jetski?
Then again, you probably haven't seen them after the divorce settlement either.

I told my son he was a disappointment.
He said, "At least I'm consistent."

My dating profile says I'm "fluent in sarcasm."
Turns out that's just depression's resume.

People keep telling me I need to "find myself."
I told them I'm not lost—I know exactly where I am. That's the problem.

I went to church for the first time in years.
The priest said, "Welcome back."
I said, "I'm just here because my life is spiraling."
He said, "So you are coming back."

My boss asked why I looked so tired.
I said, "I've been staying up thinking about all the ways this job is killing me."
He said, "Well, stop—you're billing the client."

I love my dog unconditionally.
He loves me unconditionally too.
Mostly because he has no conception of my actual personality.

My friend said he found the love of his life.
I said, "That's great!"
He said, "Yeah, we met at an AA meeting."
I said, "Oh, congratulations on getting sober!"
He said, "No, we just liked each other's stories."

I asked my mom why she never taught me to cook.
She said, "Because I wanted you to learn self-preservation."
